approximate.en: close to the actual amount but not exact

automatically.en: without conscious thought or control; by itself

beneficially.en: in a way that is helpful or produces good results

broad.en: wide; including many different people or things

careful.en: giving close attention to avoid mistakes

common.en: happening often or found in many places

compound.en: to make a problem or difficulty worse

disparage.en: to speak about someone or something as if they are not important or good

hamper.en: to prevent something from happening or moving easily

hinder.en: to make it difficult for something to happen or develop

hopeful.en: feeling or showing that you expect something good to happen

impede.en: to slow down or block the progress of something

marginal.en: small and not important; at the edge

misanthropic.en: disliking or distrusting people in general
misanthropic.zh: 厭惡人類的；憤世嫉俗的

obstruct.en: to block or get in the way of something so it cannot progress

optimistic.en: expecting that good things will happen

outlying.en: far from the center of a place

outstrip.en: to be or become greater, faster, or more successful than something else

peripheral.en: not central or most important; on the edge
peripheral.zh: 位於邊緣的；周邊的；次要的

positive.en: hopeful and confident; expecting good results

recalcitrant.en: stubbornly refusing to obey or cooperate

reflexively.en: automatically, as a reflex, without conscious thought

remote.en: far away from other places; isolated

sanguine.en: positive and confident about the future, especially in a difficult situation

spontaneously.en: without planning or outside cause; naturally

stymie.en: to block or prevent the progress of something

ubiquitous.zh: 無所不在的；普遍存在的

uncontrollably.en: in a way that cannot be stopped or managed

unobtrusive.zh: 不顯眼的；不引人注目的

widespread.en: existing or happening in many places or among many people
